name: Example: Evaluating the Floor Function in More Complex Cases
problem: Find the value of $f(x) = \dfrac{e^{\left\lfloor x+2 \right\rfloor}}{2x+1}$ at $x = 0.75.$ Round your answer to $2$ decimal places.
worked_solution:
Suppose $x$ is a real number. The greatest integer (or floor) function $\lfloor x \rfloor$ equals the greatest integer that is less than or equal to $x{:}$

$$
\lfloor x \rfloor = n,
\quad\text{where}\quad
n \leq x \lt n+1,\quad  n\in \mathbb Z
$$

Evaluating $f(x)$ at $x = 0.75,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}f(0.75) & =\frac{{e}^{⌊0.75+2⌋}}{2(0.75)+1} \\  & =\frac{{e}^{⌊2.75⌋}}{2.5}.\end{aligned}
$$

Now, from the definition of the greatest integer function, we have

$$
\left\lfloor 2.75\right\rfloor = 2.
$$

Therefore, we conclude that

$$
\begin{aligned}f(0.75) & =\frac{{e}^{⌊2.75⌋}}{2.5} \\  & =\frac{{e}^{2}}{2.5} \\  & =2.955\,62… \\  & ≈2.96,\end{aligned}
$$

rounded to $2$ decimal places.
